items.title: Five Marks of Genuine Mutual Benefit, and Why Only Present Suffering or Pleasure Never Decides Anything Alone

items.zh: 略說應知有五種相。一、無罪相，二攝受相，三、此世相，四、他世相，五、寂滅相。若諸菩薩所有自能若少若多攝受善法、增長善法；或復令他若少若多攝受善法、增長善法，勸勉、調伏、安置、建立；是名菩薩利益種類自利利他無有罪相。若諸菩薩能引所有若自若他無染污樂、或眾具樂、或住定樂、是名菩薩利益種類自利利他能攝受相。
items.en: In brief, one should know there are five such marks: blamelessness; embracing wholesome pleasure; this-life benefit; other-life benefit; and quiescence.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩自利利他，或有此世能為利益，非於他世；或有他世能為利益，非於此世；或有此世及於他世俱為利益；或有此世及於他世俱非利益。如是四種自利利他，於四法受，隨其次第，如應當知。云何名為四種法受？或有法受，現在受樂，於當來世受苦異熟；或有法受，現在受苦，於當來世受樂異熟；或有法受，現在受樂，於當來世受樂異熟；或有法受，現在受苦，於當來世受苦異熟。此四廣辯，如經應知。是名菩薩利益種類自利利他
items.en: A bodhisattva's self-benefit and benefiting others may bring benefit in this life but not the next; or in the next life but not this one; or in both; or in neither … yet a bodhisattva does not actually engage in all four of these — for a bodhisattva's self-benefit and benefiting others, the fourth case (benefiting neither life at all) should never apply.

items.title: Section: Quiescence Closes Benefit; Five Kinds of Happiness Open, from Its Distant Cause to Awakening Itself

items.zh: 若諸菩薩所有涅槃，及得涅槃世出世間涅槃分法，是名菩薩利益種類自利利他寂滅略相。當知此相望餘一切，無上最勝。
items.en: A bodhisattva's own nirvāṇa, and the mundane and supramundane factors leading to it, are, in brief, the mark of quiescence within benefit-category mutual benefit. One should know this mark surpasses all the others, unsurpassed and most excellent.

items.zh: 云何菩薩安樂種類自利利他？

略說應知五樂所攝。何等五樂？一者、因樂，二者、受樂，三者、苦對治樂，四者、受斷樂，五者、無惱害樂。言因樂者，謂二樂品諸根境界，若此為因順樂受觸，若諸所有現法當來可愛果業，如是一切總攝為一，名為因樂。除此更無若過若增。言受樂者，謂待苦息，由前所說因樂所攝三因緣故，有能攝益身心受生，名為受樂。略說此樂復有二種。一者、有漏，二者、無漏。無漏樂者，學無學樂。有漏樂者，欲、色、無色三界繫樂。又此一切三界繫樂，隨其所應六處別故，有其六種。謂眼觸所生，乃至意觸所生。如是六種復攝為二。一者、身樂，二者、心樂。五識相應，名為身樂；意識相應，名為心樂。若對治樂者，謂因寒熱飢渴等事，生起非一眾多品類種種苦受，由能對治息除寒熱飢渴等苦，即於如是苦息滅時，生起樂覺，是則名為苦對治樂。滅想受定，名受斷樂。無惱害樂，應知略說復有四種。一、出離樂，二、遠離樂，三、寂靜樂，四、三菩提樂。正信捨家，趣於非家，解脫煩籠居家迫迮種種大苦，名出離樂。斷除諸欲惡不善法，證初靜慮離生喜樂，名遠離樂。第二靜慮已上諸定，尋伺止息，名寂靜樂。一切煩惱畢竟離繫，於所知事如實等覺，此樂名為三菩提樂。
items.en: In brief, one should know this is subsumed under five kinds of happiness. What are the five? First, causal happiness; second, felt happiness; third, happiness as an antidote to suffering; fourth, happiness through the cessation of feeling; fifth, harmless happiness. Harmless happiness, in brief, is further of four kinds: the happiness of renunciation, of seclusion, of stillness, and of awakening itself.

items.title: Why Each Kind of "Happiness" Earns the Name for a Completely Different Reason

items.zh: 此中因樂，是樂因故，說名為樂。非自性故。此中受樂，樂自性故，說名為樂，非樂因故。苦對治樂，息眾苦故、遣眾苦故，說名為樂，非樂因故、非自性故。其受斷樂，非樂因故、非自性故，亦非息遣種種苦故，說名為樂。然依勝義，諸所有受皆悉是苦，住滅定時，此勝義苦暫時寂靜，故名為樂。
items.en: Causal happiness is called happiness because it is happiness's cause, not because it is happiness's own nature. Felt happiness is called happiness because it is happiness's own nature, not because it is happiness's cause. Happiness-as-antidote is called happiness because it stills and removes manifold suffering, not because it is happiness's cause or nature. Happiness through the cessation of feeling is called happiness neither because it is happiness's cause, nor its nature, nor because it removes manifold suffering — but because, in ultimate terms, every feeling whatsoever is actually suffering, and while abiding in the attainment of cessation, this ultimate suffering is, for that time, stilled — and it is for this reason called happiness.

items.zh: 無惱害樂所攝最後三菩提樂，由當來世此勝義苦永寂滅故，於現法中附在所依諸煩惱品一切麁重永寂滅故，說名為樂。諸餘所有無惱害樂，於最後樂能隨順故，是彼分故，能引彼故，當知亦名無惱害樂。此中菩薩念與眾生有利益品所有安樂，終不念與無利益品所有安樂。菩薩於此無利益品所有安樂，以無倒慧如實了知；勸諸眾生令悉捨離，隨力所能方便削奪。

blocks.text: What makes help genuine, and what "happiness" really means. A short passage (0483c24) is untranslated.
Genuine mutual benefit is: **blameless**; it **embraces wholesome happiness**; it benefits **this life**; it benefits **future lives**; it leads to **quiescence**.
Some benefit is for this life only, some for the next, some both, some neither. A bodhisattva does not engage in all four indiscriminately; what benefits this life but harms the next is rejected.
"A bodhisattva's own nirvāṇa, and the mundane and supramundane factors leading to it": this mark "surpasses all the others".

Causal; felt; happiness as an antidote to suffering; happiness through the cessation of feeling; and harmless happiness, which is of four kinds: the happiness of renunciation, of seclusion, of stillness, and of awakening itself.

Causal happiness is so called "because it is happiness's cause, not its own nature"; felt happiness "because it is happiness's own nature"; the antidote "because it stills manifold suffering". The cessation of feeling is called happiness for none of these reasons, but "because, in ultimate terms, every feeling is actually suffering, and in the attainment of cessation this ultimate suffering is, for that time, stilled".

quiz.q: Of the five marks, "blamelessness" and "embracing" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: blamelessness is about cause, embracing about fruit
quiz.why: "Blamelessness; embracing wholesome pleasure; this-life benefit; other-life benefit; and quiescence." Venerable Miào Jìng: the section on blamelessness is basically about cause; embracing is basically about fruit.

quiz.q: "Mundane and supramundane factors (分) leading to nirvāṇa." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 分?
options: 分 means cause — the cause of the fruit of nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "A bodhisattva's own nirvāṇa, and the mundane and supramundane factors leading to it, are, in brief, the mark of quiescence." Venerable Miào Jìng: in "nirvāṇa factors," 分 means cause — the cause of the fruit of nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: Among harmless happiness, "the happiness of renunciation" — what does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: renunciation is going forth — leaving home is a happiness
quiz.why: "Harmless happiness, in brief, is further of four kinds: the happiness of renunciation, of seclusion, of stillness, and of awakening itself." Master Cháng Bǎi: in short, the happiness of renunciation is going forth; leaving home is a happiness.

quiz.q: Cessation-of-feeling happiness: "ultimately every feeling is suffering; in cessation, this ultimate suffering is stilled." How do the masters explain "ultimate suffering"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: formation-suffering known only to sages; Miào Jìng: only one who realises the ultimate knows it as suffering
quiz.why: "In ultimate terms, every feeling whatsoever is actually suffering, and while abiding in the attainment of cessation, this ultimate suffering is, for that time, stilled — and it is for this reason called happiness." Master Cháng Bǎi: ultimate suffering is formation-suffering that only sages know. Venerable Miào Jìng: only those who have realised the ultimate know this is suffering!
